To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the classical learning algorithm can be made to work even if the incomplete membership oracle leaves a relatively large fraction (more than 40 percent) of the questions unanswered; and (2) the classical learning problem is not polynomially solvable if the incomplete membership oracles answer a fraction of 1/poly (n) of the questions.

(1) the obvious method for dealing with missing answers is essentially optimal; (2) a small fraction of missing answers can render the incomplete membership oracle completely useless; (3) a large fraction of missing queries can be tolerated by query learners.
(1) the obvious method of exhaustive search cannot be improved in general, and (2) the incomplete membership oracle becomes essentially useless even if it answers only a fraction 10/poly(n) queries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of what fraction of missing answers can be tolerated by query learners, and with the question of how the incomplete membership oracle should be used in order to minimize the number of unanswered queries.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a missing membership oracle cannot be rendered useless, but can be rendered inefficient.
a large fraction of missing queries can be tolerated by query learners, but only if the learner has a prior knowledge of the answer patterns associated with the unanswered questions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incomplete membership query model is a very challenging learning scenario that cannot be handled by a simple general method.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of a missing membership oracle, the learner can tolerate only a relatively small fraction of missing answers.
the incompleteness of the membership oracle can have a devastating effect on the learnability of a concept class even when the incompleteness rate is extremely low.
the model of exact learnability using an equivalence oracle (and a possibly incomplete membership oracle) is quite robust and is not affected by even a relatively high fraction of unanswered queries.
